title: Il poolish entra nell’impasto finale
target: Prefermenti · Poolish, Come si fa, passo 3
author: Eva / Electric Blue Food
caption_it: Versa il poolish nella farina e nell’acqua dell’impasto finale, recuperandolo dal recipiente con una spatola.
limits: La foto documenta poolish vero in trasferimento. Il disegno non stabilisce dosi, maturazione o una soglia di bolle; omette il marchio, il tavolo e semplifica le superfici.
scene: A smaller terracotta mixing bowl is tilted above a larger clear glass bowl containing a modest bed of flour and some water. A hand supports the small bowl from its outside, while a second hand holds a plain ivory-handled spatula INSIDE it, sweeping a broad soft cohesive ribbon of mature POOLISH over its lip. Poolish slumps under gravity toward the flour in the receiving bowl, rather than spraying like water or falling as a kneaded ball. Use photo 2 for the real viscous ribbon and the spatula-to-bowl contact. A small number of irregular openings in the ribbon suggest real aeration; no repeating bubble network or dense holes. Both entire bowls visible, upper tilted bowl at upper left, receiving bowl at lower right, a small gap between rims, the ribbon physically connecting the pouring bowl to the lower ingredients. One coherent transfer gesture. No separate ingredient cups, yeast packets, scoop or labels. Omit the photographic table and background.

title: Riprendere l’impasto dopo l’autolisi
target: Prefermenti · Autolisi, Come si fa, passo 3
author: Rebecca Eisenberg / The Practical Kitchen
caption_it: Dopo il riposo di autolisi, incorpora gli ingredienti previsti dal procedimento. La mano stringe e ripiega la massa nella ciotola.
limits: La foto originale usa sale e miscela di acqua, lievito e zucchero. Si riprende soltanto il gesto di incorporazione: la tavola non aggiunge zucchero alla procedura di Vulcan e non prescrive quantità o un ordine universale.
scene: One whole clear glass mixing bowl, three-quarter overhead view, containing a rough connected ivory dough mass at the beginning of final incorporation after an autolyse rest. ONE realistic hand enters from upper right and forms a broad pincer: thumb on the near side, four curved fingers on the far side, gently squeezing through a short thick band of the dough. The working hand stays inside the bowl's rim and its finger contact visibly indents the mass; the dough is supported by the bottom of the bowl. Use photo2 for the actual pinch-through contact and folded rough connected dough, simplified to a few broad folds and long contours. A thin sheen of mixing water at the base is enough, no puddles, no scattered salt crystals or flour speckling, no separate ingredient cups. The dough is neither a perfect ball nor torn into many detached pieces. No decorative bubbles, thick creamy sauce, foam or fake silky swirls. Just the hand, bowl and partly mixed dough, with warm terracotta accents in the outlines.

title: Sostenere la pasta sul dorso delle mani
target: Problemi e soluzioni · P02/P16, prevenzione durante la stesura
author: Rebecca Eisenberg / The Practical Kitchen
caption_it: Il dorso delle mani sostiene la pasta durante l’allargamento, distribuendo il peso senza puntare le dita nel centro. Se oppone resistenza, appoggiala e lasciala riposare.
limits: Il riferimento mostra un momento della stesura con una mano più alta e una che sostiene il bordo inferiore. Non si rappresenta un lancio in aria né una misura dello spessore. Una posa credibile, non una riparazione del buco.
scene: A single large thin pizza dough disc draped over the BACKS of two hands, shown in a clear oblique side view. Follow photo2's actual pose: left-side upper forearm supports the upper part over the back of a gently curved hand, the second forearm enters from lower left and its hand supports the lower side of the sheet from underneath. The dough hangs as one broad continuous curved sheet with a slightly thicker rounded rim, while its bottom edge just rests on the work level. Both hands are beneath/behind the sheet, fingertips curved away from its thin centre, no fingernail or fingertip protrudes through it. Hands carry rather than pinch or tear the dough, gravity makes the drape. Simplify the dough to a clean warm ivory surface with broad gentle folds at contact points. No ripped hole, no windowpane test, no stretched noodle strands, no veil mesh, no pizza tossed into air, no rolling pin, no bowl, no countertop rectangle or scattered flour. Keep the whole dough disc within the canvas; forearms may end near left margin. The surface is matte with only long clean brown contours.
